column1: prompt
Write a brief apology email to a customer whose order was delayed by two weeks due to a warehouse issue. Offer a 15% discount on their next purchase.
Draft a welcome email for a new SaaS subscriber. Include onboarding steps, a link to the help center, and a prompt to book a customer success call.
Compose a reference request email asking a former manager if they'd be willing to serve as a professional reference for a new job application.
Write a newsletter unsubscribe acknowledgment email that is warm, non-guilt-tripping, and offers a preference center link.
Draft a follow-up email sequence (3 emails, one per week) for a lead who downloaded a whitepaper but hasn't booked a demo.
Summarize the key plot points of a three-act story structure in under 200 words, as if briefing a film producer.
Condense a 10-page employee handbook section on PTO policy into a single-page FAQ suitable for new hires.
Write a plain-language summary of a clinical trial abstract about a new hypertension medication for a patient audience.
Summarize the key differences between supervised and unsupervised machine learning in three sentences for a non-technical executive.
Write five Instagram captions for a specialty coffee brand's new single-origin Ethiopian pour-over. Vary tone from sensory to storytelling.
Draft a Reddit post for r/personalfinance asking for advice on whether to pay off a student loan early or invest the extra cash in index funds.
Create a YouTube video description for a 10-minute tutorial on how to set up a personal Notion dashboard for weekly planning.
Write a product description for a standing desk converter targeting remote workers with limited space. Highlight ergonomic benefits.
Draft three A/B test variants of a CTA button label for a SaaS pricing page. The goal is free trial signups.
Write a 50-word tagline and one-sentence value proposition for a fintech app that rounds up purchases and invests the spare change.
Write an incident report template for a software outage. Include fields for timeline, root cause, impact, and preventive measures.
Draft a one-page status update memo for stakeholders on a delayed product launch, explaining the cause and revised timeline.
Write a job description for a mid-level data analyst role at a fintech startup. Include must-haves and nice-to-haves separately.
Draft a performance improvement plan (PIP) cover letter that is firm but empathetic, outlining expectations and support offered.
Write the opening paragraph of a cozy mystery novel set in a Scottish seaside town where the local librarian discovers a body in the rare books room.
Compose a limerick about the existential dread of receiving a calendar invite for a meeting that could have been an email.
Write a short horror story (under 300 words) where the monster is unreliable Wi-Fi during a critical video job interview.
Explain the difference between margin and markup to a first-year business student using a concrete example from a bakery.
Write an ELI5 explanation of how HTTPS encryption works, using an analogy appropriate for a curious 12-year-old.
Create a study guide outline for the causes of World War I, suitable for a high school history exam.
Write API documentation for a single REST endpoint: POST /users/register. Include request body schema, success response, and common error codes.
Draft a README.md for a personal open-source CLI tool that converts Markdown files to styled HTML. Include installation and usage sections.
Write a plain-English privacy policy section explaining what cookies are collected on a blog and why.
Draft a remote work policy for a 50-person company covering core hours, equipment reimbursement, and communication expectations.
Write a product origin story for a fictional hot sauce brand founded by a retired firefighter. Under 200 words. Warm, punchy, made for the About page.
Write a concise onboarding checklist for a new backend engineer joining a Python/Django team. Cover: repo setup, local dev environment, code review process, and first-week goals.
Write a networking email to a speaker you admired at a conference, referencing a specific point they made and proposing a 20-minute virtual coffee chat.
Write a TL;DR (under 100 words) for a lengthy Reddit thread debating whether TypeScript is worth the overhead for small teams.
Write a 280-character tweet announcing a personal project: an open-source Python library for parsing Indian legal documents. Make it technically credible and inviting to contributors.
Write a feature announcement for a browser extension's changelog: the new feature detects passive voice in writing and suggests active alternatives.
Write a weekly team update (5 bullet points) for an engineering team that shipped a new authentication module, fixed 3 bugs, and is blocked on a design review.
Write a glossary of 10 key terms every first-year economics student needs to know. Each definition should be one to two sentences.
Write a mock Yelp review (3 stars) for a time travel service that works perfectly but always sends you somewhere slightly inconvenient.
Write an announcement email to the whole company introducing a new flexible PTO policy. Keep it under 150 words. Warm, clear, no HR jargon.
Write a LinkedIn recommendation for a product designer who is brilliant at simplifying complex workflows but sometimes misses deadlines. Be honest and still glowing.
Write release notes for a Node.js package v2.0.0 that introduces a breaking change: callback-based API replaced with async/await. Include migration instructions.
Write a vendor rejection email after a procurement process. Be professional, non-specific about reasons, and leave the door open for future engagement.
Write a one-paragraph summary of the book 'Thinking, Fast and Slow' suitable for a Goodreads review by a business professional.
Write the opening two sentences of five different genre novels all set in the same location: a broken-down vending machine in a Bangalore office lobby.
Write a push notification copy (under 60 characters) for five different moments in a fitness app: workout reminder, goal achieved, streak at risk, new challenge, and rest day.
Explain what a p-value is using an analogy involving a courtroom, for a product manager who has never taken a statistics course.
Write a code of conduct for an open-source project covering: inclusive language, conflict resolution, contribution guidelines, and enforcement process. Keep it under 400 words.
Write a monthly metrics email to investors covering: MRR growth, churn, NPS change, and one key qualitative insight. The numbers are mixed — be transparent but not alarmist.
Write a rejection email to a job candidate who interviewed well but was not selected. Be warm, specific about next steps, and avoid empty platitudes.
Write three completely different 30-second radio ad scripts for the same product: a noise-canceling sleep mask. Vary tone: funny, emotional, rational.
Write a comment block for a complex Python function that implements Dijkstra's algorithm. Include: purpose, parameters, return value, time complexity, and a usage example.
Write a pitch email to a podcast host proposing yourself as a guest. The topic: lessons learned from building and shutting down a startup. Under 200 words.
Summarize the key arguments for and against cryptocurrency as a store of value in three bullet points each. Neutral tone.
Write five tweet variations for announcing that your company just crossed $1M ARR. Vary from humble to bold to data-driven.
Write an error message for a failed payment that is honest about what went wrong, tells the user exactly what to do next, and doesn't make them feel bad.
Write a FAQ (5 questions) about mRNA vaccines suitable for a community health center's patient-facing website. Plain English, no condescension.
Write a Slack message template a team lead should send when a production incident is resolved. Include: what happened, who was affected, what was done, and what's next.
Write a rejection letter from a fictional colony on Mars to a highly qualified Earth engineer, citing 'cultural fit' concerns. Play it completely straight.
Write a one-page executive summary for a business case proposing a switch from Salesforce to HubSpot for a 150-person company. Include cost savings, migration risks, and recommendation.
Write an end-of-sprint retrospective summary covering: what went well, what didn't, three action items, and team morale signal. Fictional but realistic details.
Write a professional email declining a speaking invitation due to schedule conflicts, while genuinely recommending two alternative speakers with brief intros.
Write the blurb for the back cover of a debut thriller novel about a forensic accountant who discovers a money laundering scheme hidden inside a charity's carbon offset program.
Write a breakup email ending a freelance client relationship. The client has been slow to pay and keeps expanding scope. Be professional, clear, and leave no ambiguity.
Write a CONTRIBUTING.md guide for an open-source data science library. Cover: branch naming, commit message convention, test requirements, documentation standards, and PR review SLA.
Write a BLUF (bottom line up front) one-paragraph memo summarizing why a proposed office relocation to a different city should not proceed. Address three key concerns.
Write five microcopy strings for error states in a mobile payment app: card declined, network timeout, incorrect PIN, amount exceeds limit, and recipient not found. Each under 15 words.
Write a plain-English explanation of what a neural network is, using an analogy to how a person learns to recognize dogs after seeing many examples.
Write a performance review for a fictional employee named 'Entropy' who consistently destroys order, misses deadlines, but somehow delivers results at the last possible moment.
Write an email to an employee addressing repeated tardiness. Maintain warmth, state clear expectations, and explain consequences without being threatening.

Write the executive summary of an IT security audit report that found two critical vulnerabilities (exposed API keys in public GitHub repo, unpatched server with CVE score 9.1) and seven medium-severity issues.
Write a Twitter/X thread (6 tweets) explaining why most B2B SaaS demos fail and what founders should do instead.
Write a one-page business case for purchasing a ₹2 lakh ergonomic chair for the CEO, framing it as a productivity and retention investment rather than a luxury expense.
Write the 'Architecture Overview' section of a system design wiki page for a microservices-based e-commerce platform. Include a component list and brief description of each service's responsibility.
Explain the concept of compound interest to a 16-year-old using a story about investing ₹1,000 per month from age 20 versus age 30.
Write three distinct opening lines for a short story, each beginning the same event (a phone rings at 3am) but in three different genres: thriller, literary fiction, and romantic comedy.

Write a social media policy for employees of a public hospital. Cover: what can and cannot be shared about patients, how to handle negative comments about the hospital, personal vs. professional accounts, and consequences of violations.
Write an onboarding tooltip sequence (5 tooltips) for a project management tool's Kanban board. Each under 25 words. Progressive disclosure — start simple, add complexity.
Write a cheat sheet of SQL window functions (ROW_NUMBER, RANK, DENSE_RANK, LAG, LEAD, NTILE, FIRST_VALUE) with one-line descriptions and a minimal example for each.
Write a set of fortune cookie messages (10 total) targeted specifically at software engineers dealing with legacy codebases.
Write a post-event report template for a company all-hands meeting. Include sections for: key announcements, Q&A highlights, employee sentiment pulse, and follow-up action items.
Write an email to your team announcing that you are going on parental leave for 3 months. Share handover plan, point of contact for key areas, and genuine personal sentiment.

Write a developer changelog post for a breaking API change: the authentication endpoint is moving from /auth to /v2/auth and the response format is changing. Include migration deadline and code examples before/after.

Write a one-page partnership proposal outline for two complementary SaaS companies (a CRM and an email marketing tool) exploring an integration partnership. Cover: mutual value, technical integration scope, commercial model, and next steps.
Write a LinkedIn post by a first-generation immigrant engineer reflecting on their 10-year journey from arriving with no network to leading a team of 20. Authentic, not inspirational porn.
Write the terms and conditions for a fictional 'Soul Transfer' service in the style of a modern SaaS EULA. Include standard legal language applied absurdly to supernatural services.
Write a documentation page explaining how to handle pagination correctly in a REST API, covering: offset pagination, cursor pagination, keyset pagination — with code examples in Python for each.
Write a meeting agenda and pre-read for a quarterly business review between a SaaS vendor and an enterprise customer. Structure it to surface problems early and end with forward-looking planning.
Write an email declining a job offer graciously after accepting verbally the previous week. Acknowledge the awkwardness, be honest without over-explaining, and keep the relationship intact.
Write a one-page summary of the key principles in 'The Lean Startup' (Eric Ries) targeted at a product manager who has 5 minutes to read it.

Write a structured agenda for a 30-minute 1:1 meeting between a manager and a direct report who has been underperforming. Include prompts for the manager, space for the employee's perspective, and a closing action item section.
Write a follow-up email to a client who missed a scheduled demo call. Keep it short, non-pushy, and offer two reschedule options.
Draft an out-of-office auto-reply for a two-week vacation. Include who to contact for urgent matters.
Write a cold outreach email to a potential B2B customer introducing a SaaS expense management tool. Subject line included.
Write a polite but firm payment reminder email for an invoice that is 30 days overdue.
Compose a thank-you email to a job interviewer after a technical interview for a senior backend role.
Summarize the following meeting transcript in 5 bullet points, focusing only on decisions made and action items assigned.
Write a one-paragraph executive summary of a quarterly sales report where revenue grew 12% but customer churn increased by 3%.
Summarize this product changelog for non-technical users in plain English. Focus on what changed for them, not how.
Write three LinkedIn post options announcing a new product feature launch. Each under 150 words. Vary the tone: professional, conversational, story-driven.
Write a Twitter/X thread (5 tweets) explaining why most productivity systems fail and what to do instead.
Write product description copy for a standing desk with adjustable height, targeting remote workers. Max 120 words.
Write three subject line options for a promotional email announcing a 48-hour flash sale on a software subscription.
Write a short FAQ section (5 questions) for a food delivery app's help center covering order tracking and refunds.
Write clear installation instructions for a Python CLI tool that requires Python 3.10+, a virtual environment, and a .env file setup.
Write a README introduction section for an open-source GitHub project — a REST API for currency conversion.
Write a job description for a mid-level data analyst role at a fintech startup. Include responsibilities, required skills, and a note on culture.
Write an employee onboarding welcome message from the CEO to be sent on their first day.
Write a simple non-disclosure agreement (NDA) for a freelance contractor working on a confidential app prototype. Plain English, not legal jargon.
Write a 200-word origin story for a fictional coffee brand called 'Meridian Roast' that sources beans from three continents.
Write tagline options (5) for a mental health journaling app targeting young professionals.
